items.title: HybridResearcher: Bridging the Structured-Unstructured Boundary for Deep Research Agents
items.abstract: While LLM agents are increasingly capable of gathering and synthesizing evidence from a single homogeneous source, such as structured tables or unstructured data, real-world analytical questions frequently span heterogeneous sources. For example, answering one enterprise question may require both a result computed over an internal database and evidence found on the web. Recent evaluations on benchmarks like HybridDeepResearch show that even frontier agents struggle when evidence must cross this boundary. While these benchmarks have exposed the limitation, methodologies to explicitly teach cross-source reasoning remain absent. To address this, we introduce HybridResearcher, a 4B agent trained to bridge evidence across the structured and unstructured boundary. To build it, we synthesize cross-source bridge trajectories by starting with validated single-source tasks-such as existing text-to-SQL or web search queries-and fabricating the missing source around a bridge entity drawn from the seed's own output. We retain a sample only when strict construction gates confirm that neither side alone suffices, ensuring the data requires true cross-source interdependence. Finally, we train on this curated dataset using supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning. Evaluated on the existing HybridDeepResearch benchmark, HybridResearcher improves over our base model, Qwen3.5-4B, by 30.0 points pass@8 and surpasses the far larger Qwen3.5-397B-A17B by 8.3 points, while also improving over its base model on established, held-out single-source benchmarks (BrowseComp and BrowseComp-Plus), demonstrating that this complex cross-source reasoning can be taught directly to small models without triggering catastrophic forgetting.

items.abstract: Background: International airport staff play a crucial role in preventing the international spread of infectious diseases.Adequate knowledge, positive attitudes and appropriate practices (KAP) are essential for effective implementation of infection prevention and control measures.Just a simple health education intervention could make a difference in improving awareness and daily preventive behaviours among airport staff which must be evaluated.Objective: to evaluate the impact of a health education program on COVID knowledge, attitudes and practices among Assiut International airport staff and to identify predictors of post-intervention KAP scores.Methods: An intervention study was conducted among 229 staff members at Assiut International Airport, Egypt.Data were collected using a structured interviewer-administered questionnaire consisted of socio-demographic characteristics, history of COVID infection and KAP regarding COVID and infection prevention and control measures.Results: The mean age of participants was 37.40 ± 9.09 years, with 84.7% were males.Nearly 60% had direct contact with travellers during work.The mean knowledge, attitude, and practice scores improved significantly following the intervention (P-value < 0.001).Educational level, occupation and pre-intervention knowledge score independently predicted post-intervention knowledge.Pre-intervention attitude score was the only predictor of post-intervention attitude, whereas educational level and pre-intervention practice score independently predicted post-intervention practice.Conclusion and recommendations: the health education significantly improved COVID related knowledge, attitudes and practices among airport staff.Educational interventions should be integrated into routine occupational health programs to strengthen preparedness for future infectious disease outbreaks at points of entry.

items.title: Insights Concerning Situation Awareness From Airport Personnel During Routine and High-Demand Events
items.abstract: This study surveyed how airport employees perceive and maintain situation awareness (SA) during both routine and high-demand events. Fourteen airport employees across departments (Administrative and Operational) were interviewed to identify the differences across environmental/personal/organizational factors and SA culture that may not be visible to external observers. Both quantitative and qualitative measures were collected throughout the interview questions. A two-way mixed (SA culture × Group Position) ANOVA was conducted to identify differences of SA culture between the two position groups. No significant differences were found between the position groups. Regarding differences in SA culture, results indicated that department’s priority for SA was significantly higher than both the participants’ confidence in maintaining SA and their perceived training adequacy. Responses to qualitative questions were evaluated through word cloud generation. Different key words were identifiable in response to the two SA themes explored in the interview questions. Words like “monitoring,” “experience,” “confidence,” and “priority” were used widely throughout the responses from the employees. Combining quantitative and qualitative results, the study recognized the opportunity in the industry to identify perceived SA priority and training adequacy within organizations. Insights regarding implications to other airports with higher passenger traffic are discussed in conclusion.

items.title: INSTRUCTIONAL DESIGN OF A WORKPLACE-ORIENTED GENERAL AIGC COURSE IN THE ERA OF DIGITAL INTELLIGENCE
items.abstract: In the era of digital intelligence, artificial intelligence generated content (AIGC) has become deeply integrated into workplace workflows. However, a growing gap has emerged between corporate demand for AIGC-driven productivity and the lag in talent development. Current introductory AIGC courses suffer from fragmented content, superficial assessment methods, and limited adaptability. To address these challenges, this study proposes a holistic instructional design framework based on the "structural reconstruction, capability building, and closed-loop evaluation" model, featuring an 8-hour modular curriculum: prompt engineering (2 hours) to establish foundational concepts for cross-domain transfer, core tool mastery (4 hours) covering four mainstream AI platforms (ERNIE Bot, DeepSeek, WPS AI, and Doubao), and role-specific applications (2 hours) offering tailored practical exercises across five key professions (finance, education, software development, copywriting, and design). The framework employs a hybrid assessment model combining self-evaluations, instructor feedback, and AI-driven evaluations to target real-world problem-solving skills and adaptability to new tools, while a data-driven feedback loop enables continuous optimization of both course content and personalized learning interventions. Ultimately, this study provides a scalable, iterative system framework for empowering today's AI-driven workforce.

items.title: Integrating Agrometeorology, Agronomy and Artificial Intelligence for Climate-Resilient Sustainable Food Production: A Critical Narrative Review
items.abstract: Climate-resilient food production requires decisions that are meteorologically informed, agronomically plausible and adaptive to rapidly changing conditions. Agrometeorology provides observations and forecasts of weather and climate risk; agronomy translates those risks into crop, soil and management responses; and artificial intelligence can fuse high-volume, heterogeneous data, learn complex relationships and accelerate prediction. These domains are increasingly connected, yet their evidence bases remain partly fragmented. This critical narrative review evaluates how their integration can support sustainable crop production, with particular attention to the chain from environmental observation and prediction to management action and measurable resilience outcomes. Literature published from 1 January 2000 to 8 August 2026 was examined through relevant agricultural, multidisciplinary and biomedical scholarly sources, with supplementary citation searching and verification of bibliographic metadata. The synthesis shows that the strongest case for integration is not a replacement of process knowledge by data-driven prediction, but a division of labour: meteorological models define time-varying hazard, agronomic models constrain biological plausibility and management options, and artificial intelligence improves data fusion, bias correction, pattern recognition and computational efficiency. Evidence is comparatively mature for remote sensing, yield prediction and process-based crop modelling, and is rapidly advancing for machine-learned weather prediction. By contrast, end-to-end demonstrations that connect forecast skill to farm decisions, yield stability, resource-use efficiency, profitability and environmental outcomes remain limited. Hybrid crop-model and machine-learning approaches are promising, but uncertainty calibration, domain shift, sparse ground truth, interoperability, digital inequality and data governance remain substantial constraints. Digital twins offer a useful integration architecture, although agricultural implementations are still less mature than the concept implies. Future research should prioritise multi-environment prospective validation, decision-centred forecast verification, causal evaluation of management recommendations, uncertainty-aware hybrid modelling and equitable deployment. The most defensible conclusion is that integration can improve climate resilience only when predictive accuracy is coupled to agronomic actionability, transparent uncertainty and outcome-based evaluation.

items.title: Integrating AI for Hyperpersonalised Automotive Products and Services
items.abstract: This chapter examines how artificial intelligence can support hyperpersonalisation across automotive products and services. It adopts a conceptual, document-based approach, using dated manufacturer publications to illustrate comfort settings, conversational interfaces and proactive after-sales support. It distinguishes customer-selected customisation, stored preferences and AI-supported inference, since a personalised function does not necessarily use AI. The discussion develops a proposed management framework linking a customer task, suitable data, a recommendation, user control and evaluation. It considers drivers, passengers, vehicle owners and dealership staff across purchase, use and service. Potential commercial benefits remain propositions requiring evidence; manufacturer descriptions do not establish improvements in loyalty, conversion, satisfaction or safety. The chapter also addresses privacy, shared vehicles, data quality, fairness and excessive personalisation. It proposes future evaluation of specific automotive tasks rather than reporting a completed survey or experiment. The main implication is that automotive personalisation should be assessed through usefulness, understandable control and reliable service delivery, with commercial measures interpreted alongside customer outcomes.

items.title: Integration of AI in Education Toward Future-Ready Assessments
items.abstract: This research examines the dual impact of artificial intelligence in education, in response to the rapid development of AI technologies. The study explores how AI can enhance learning efficiency and educational outcomes while presenting challenges to academic integrity and fundamental skills development. Employing a mixed-methods approach, the study involved 44 EFL students in Oman and surveyed 102 students from various educational institutions. Researchers analyzed students’ performance in both AI-assisted and traditional writing tasks while observing behavioral patterns and attitudes toward these technologies. Key findings revealed a 42% reduction in grammatical errors with AI assistance, yet 63% of students failed to fully follow instructions, demonstrating limited deep content understanding. While 91% of students reported using AI tools, 60.4% expressed the need for training in ethical usage. The study concludes with three critical recommendations: developing clear institutional policies for AI governance, redesigning assessment methods to focus on learning processes rather than products and strengthening academic values and transparency. These proposals align with the vision of balancing innovation with adaptation to technological change.

items.title: Integration of Auditory and Tactile Information in Time-to-Contact Estimation
items.abstract: This study investigated the integration of auditory and tactile information in time-to-contact (TTC) estimation for objects moving with constant velocity (Experiment 1) and constant acceleration (Experiment 2). Participants estimated TTC using a prediction-motion task under auditory, tactile, and audio-tactile conditions to determine whether people can use vibrotactile stimuli to judge TTC and whether concurrent cues improve judgments compared to single modalities. Analyses of absolute constant error revealed a sensory modality effect in Experiment 2, where audio-tactile stimuli produced lower error than tactile alone, but not in Experiment 1. Variable error showed greater audio-tactile precision over tactile-only stimuli across both experiments, though audio-tactile performance never differed from auditory-only cues. These findings are consistent with the revised tau theory, in which people combine first-order information from several sources to make TTC estimations.

items.title: Inteligência artificial na educação e neuroplasticidade: contribuições, limites e desafios para a aprendizagem
items.abstract: The literature on artificial intelligence (AI) in education focuses almost exclusively on performance, perception, and engagement; brain changes associated with neuroplasticity have rarely been measured. This narrative review, using explicit search and classification criteria, distinguishes three types of evidence: (a) learning outcomes (grades, retention, and transfer), (b) behavioral measures of cognitive effort, and (c) direct neurophysiological measures (EEG and fNIRS). The most robust performance studies indicate that the effects of AI depend on task design: a randomized trial involving approximately one thousand high school students found gains ranging from 48% to 127% during AI-assisted practice, while performance declined on an exam taken without AI among students with unrestricted access to the model; this decline was eliminated when the system was configured to provide hints rather than answers. The most frequently cited meta-analysis supporting AI (g = 0.867) was retracted in 2026 due to analytical errors and the inclusion of invalid studies. The few studies using brain-based measures are small (n ranging from 24 to 54), short in duration, unpublished in peer-reviewed journals or reporting null findings, and assess momentary engagement rather than lasting structural or functional plasticity. It is therefore concluded that there is no basis for claiming that AI, by itself, either enhances or impairs neuroplasticity. The evidence supports a narrower conclusion: activities that replace retrieval and elaborative effort tend to reduce measured learning, whereas activities that preserve such effort tend to maintain or enhance learning gains. A research agenda is proposed incorporating longitudinal designs, transfer measures, and pre- and post-intervention neuroimaging with active control conditions.

items.title: Intelligent Academic Software: Transforming Higher Education through AI-Driven Learning Ecosystems
items.abstract: The digital transformation of higher education has accelerated with the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies into academic software systems. Intelligent Academic Software (IAS) represents a paradigm shift from static learning management systems toward dynamic, data-driven learning ecosystems capable of personalization, predictive analytics, automated assessment, and institutional decision support. This study proposes a comprehensive AI-driven learning ecosystem model integrating adaptive learning engines, intelligent tutoring systems, predictive analytics modules, and administrative automation frameworks. A multi-institutional dataset comprising 1,200 student records was analyzed using supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms to evaluate performance prediction, engagement analytics, and risk detection accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate improved academic performance forecasting (92% accuracy), enhanced learner engagement, and optimized resource allocation. The study contributes to AI-enabled higher education transformation by presenting a scalable intelligent software architecture aligned with ethical AI governance and institutional digital strategies.

items.title: INTELLIGENT WEBSITE ASSEMBLY FACTORY
items.abstract: "Intelligent Website Assembly Factory: Student Knowledge OS" là một bản tuyên ngôn sư phạm và kiến trúc hệ thống, được tác giả S.S. DuyMT biên soạn vào tháng 10/2026. Tác phẩm định hình lại vai trò của người học trong kỷ nguyên AI: chuyển dịch từ *người tiêu thụ thông tin* trở thành **Knowledge Architect (Kiến trúc sư tri thức)** của chính mình. Tác phẩm chỉ ra "nghịch lý của thời đại số": sinh viên sở hữu lượng dữ liệu khổng lồ nhưng lại thiếu vắng một cấu trúc tri thức (Knowledge Base) vững chắc. Triết lý cốt lõi được đề xuất là: *AI càng mạnh, con người càng cần một kiến trúc tư duy mạnh*. Thay vì xây dựng những website/portfolio rời rạc, tác phẩm giới thiệu mô hình **Knowledge OS** (Hệ điều hành tri thức cá nhân) – một hạ tầng số lưu giữ lịch sử tiến hóa tư duy, kết nối các môn học, dự án và bản sắc trí tuệ suốt đời. Để hiện thực hóa điều này ở quy mô lớn, tác giả đề xuất kiến trúc **Intelligent Website Assembly Factory** (Nhà máy lắp ráp Website thông minh) dựa trên giao thức SBBS 3.0, với các trụ cột chính: * **Chuyển dịch tư duy:** Từ "Code First" sang "Structure First"; từ "Technology First" sang "Knowledge First".* **Giao thức SBBS 3.0:** Áp dụng triết lý *"Contract trước, Code sau"*, phân rã hệ thống thành các "Smart Box" và "Capability" để AI Agent có thể khám phá, so khớp và lắp ráp tự động (Composable Intelligence).* **GitHub như hạ tầng tri thức:** Biến Repository thành "cuốn sách đang sống", Commit thành "lịch sử tư duy", và Markdown/JSON thành ngôn ngữ kết nối giữa người và AI.* **Bản sắc số (Digital Intellectual Identity):** Factory cung cấp khung kiến trúc chung, nhưng sinh viên cung cấp "bản sắc", tạo ra những Knowledge OS độc bản, trường tồn cùng sự nghiệp. Đây là tài liệu nền tảng dành cho các nhà nghiên cứu giáo dục, nhà phát triển AI Agent, và đặc biệt là sinh viên – những người muốn xây dựng một "bản sắc số" có khả năng sinh trưởng suốt đời.

items.title: Interpretable Deep Multimodal Fusion of ECG and Facial Expressions for Robust Emotion Detection
items.abstract: In healthcare, emotional computing, and dynamic human-computer interaction, emotion recognition is a key component of human-centric Artificial Intelligence (AI). However, existing approaches depend on either physiological or visual signals and often show limited robustness or accuracy in noisy or inadequate data environments. This study proposes a task-specific bidirectional cross-modal fusion framework in which physiological ECG representations and facial-expression representations mutually attend to each other, while an auxiliary embedding-alignment objective constrains the two modalities to a shared latent space. While the facial images are processed using EfficientNet-B0 to extract discriminative visual features, the ECG signals are transformed using a one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN) in conjunction with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) network to extract local morphological features and long-range temporal inference. A cross-attention fusion technique is then used to fuse the trained ECG models with facial expression data. The inter-modal dependencies between physiological and behavioral signals are represented by a cross-attention fusion module, which improves the model's dependability and broadens its capacity to identify a variety of emotional classes, specifically focusing on six fundamental emotions: happy, sad, angry, fearful, surprised, and neutral. The acquired representation is classified using a fully connected attention-based decoder. Model interpretability is attained through SHAP analysis of ECG embeddings and Grad-CAM visualization of the facial areas. When compared to current and baseline fusion techniques, the evaluation conducted using the MAHNOB-HCI and AMIGOS datasets demonstrated that the proposed model achieved higher performance, including an accuracy of 97%, precision of 96%, recall of 97%, F1-score of 96%, and improved adaptability.

items.title: Investigating the Impact of AI-Facilitated Socratic Dialogue on Critical Thinking Skills
items.abstract: This mixed-method study aims to explore the impact of having Socratic dialogue with artificial intelligence (AI) on students' critical thinking skills’ performance. The data were gathered from 35 foundation-level students. The study utilised a Watson Glaser critical thinking pre-test and post-test to measure their critical thinking abilities and a questionnaire to gather their perception of AI usage. During the intervention, students were engaged in structured AI-facilitated Socratic questioning sessions weekly. Data were analysed using paired-sample t-tests and linear regression, while survey responses were examined for thematic trends. Even though the data collected shows that students have a positive perception of using AI, there is no statistically significant difference between the pre- and post-tests (p > .05). The finding shows that students’ critical thinking performance did not improve throughout the study. Furthermore, the results for the linear regression (R² = 0.038, p > .05) show that there is very little correlation between students’ perception and their critical thinking performance. The study reveals the gap between students’ positive perception of using AI and their critical thinking skill development.

items.title: Ionizable Lipid Nanoparticles as a siRNA Delivery Carrier: A Review
items.abstract: Abstract Small interfering RNA (siRNA)-based gene silencing has evolved as a promising strategy for treating a wide range of human diseases. However, naked siRNA molecules are susceptible to degradation by cellular nucleases, immune activation, and rapid renal clearance. Therefore, various siRNA delivery vectors have been developed, among which lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have received significant attention due to their excellent biocompatibility and low immunogenicity. Conventionally, permanent cationic lipids were used for the fabrication of LNPs, but their clinical translation was limited by cytotoxicity, immunogenicity, and non-specific interactions. To overcome these limitations, significant progress has been made in developing advanced LNPs using ionizable lipids (ILs) (termed as IL nanoparticles or iLNPs) that are neutral at physiological pH but acquire a positive charge in the acidic endosomal compartments, thereby minimizing toxicity and facilitating efficient endosomal escape. This review summarizes the different vectors for siRNA delivery, the evolution of iLNPs, their composition, and surface modification strategies. Furthermore, we discuss the application of iLNP-mediated siRNA therapy for several human diseases, including an FDA-approved therapy. Finally, we highlight the current challenges of iLNP-based siRNA therapeutics and possible artificial intelligence-guided approaches for the rational design and development of next-generation iLNPs for effective siRNA delivery.

items.title: LANGUAGE DEVELOPMENT: NEOLOGISMS IN CONTEMPORARY ENGLISH
items.abstract: Language development is a continuous process shaped by social transformation, technological innovation, cultural interaction, and changes in human communication. One of the most significant manifestations of this process is the emergence of neologisms, which are newly created words or expressions, as well as existing words that acquire new meanings. In contemporary English, neologisms emerge in response to developments in digital technology, artificial intelligence, social media, science, popular culture, and global communication. This article examines the role of neologisms in the development of modern English, focusing on their formation, classification, dissemination, and influence on vocabulary expansion. Particular attention is given to word formation processes such as compounding, blending, affixation, abbreviation, borrowing, and semantic change. The article also considers the role of digital communication in popularising new lexical items and discusses the challenges associated with their interpretation, standardisation, and long-term acceptance. The analysis demonstrates that neologisms reflect the changing needs of English speakers and contribute significantly to the flexibility and expressive potential of the language.

items.title: Large language models for depression assessment from brief daily diaries
items.abstract: Abstract Closely tracking changes in depression is important for clinical research and practice. However, intensive longitudinal depression assessment relies on self-report surveys that have major limitations. Scoring depression from natural language with large language models (LLMs) could resolve these shortcomings. This study tested the validity of depression rated by LLMs from daily video diaries. We studied 108 participants selected for mental health treatment status (45% in treatment). Participants completed a clinical interview and 14-21 days of depression surveys and video diaries. Daily depression scores were estimated by LLMs from diary transcripts. LLM ratings converged with self-report depression within-person ( r = .45;95% CrI[.40, .49]) and when averaged across days for an overall depression score ( r = .61;95% CrI[.43,.75]). Averaged LLM ratings correlated with depression symptom severity ascertained by clinical interview ( r = .53;95% CrI[.35, .68]). LLM-rated depression and self-report had similar profiles of associations with daily functioning variables (profile r = .98 within-person; r = .94 between-person). Multivariable regression results showed LLM ratings predicted daily functioning variables (partial $$\beta s$$ β s =|.12 | - | .28 | ) and interview-rated depression (partial $$\beta$$ β =.33;95% CrI[.07, .58]) over and above self-reports, suggesting LLMs capture clinically-relevant information that self-reports miss. Findings establish a strong foundation for a depression assessment approach that addresses shortcomings of self-reports while satisfying the unique demands of intensive longitudinal monitoring.

items.title: Large language models on tabular data based molecular property prediction (MPP) of RP-3 kerosene
items.abstract: Accurate modeling of multicomponent fuel properties is important for surrogate fuel design, where complex composition-property relationships motivate the development of advanced data-driven prediction strategies. In this study, we evaluate pretrained molecular and general-purpose language model representations for predicting physiochemically distinct properties of RP-3 kerosene surrogates using SMILES-derived embeddings and composition-based information. Four supervised machine learning (ML) models (SVM, GPR, RF and k-NN) were compared with three transformer-based representations (ChemBERTa, MolFormer and TinyLlama (1.1B)) across different dataset configurations. The results demonstrate that the predictive performance depends on both dataset size and feature representation strategy. For the 1000-sample dataset, TinyLlama achieved stable predictive performance (average R 2 = 0.9962), whereas the expanded 6000-sample dataset enabled ChemBERTa to achieve high prediction accuracy, explaining 99% of the property variance (RMSE = 0.126, MRE = 0.18%) outperforming both MolFormer and TinyLlama. Notably, TinyLlama lacking any chemistry specific pretraining, still achieves R 2 = 0.995, purely from serialized composition and structured prompts, demonstrating that contextual language embeddings can encode chemically meaningful information within the investigated RP-3 surrogate fuel system. Cosine similarity and residual analyses confirm that the pretrained representations capture meaningful differences between aromatic and saturated hydrocarbon structures while maintaining strong predictive stability. The controlled ablation study further demonstrates that composition information alone provides highly accurate prediction within the investigated surrogate system, while molecular embeddings provide additional chemically informed representation capability. These findings establish a framework for evaluating pretrained molecular and language-model representations for RP-3 surrogate fuel property prediction, with potential extension toward broader hydrocarbon fuel systems after validation using more diverse molecular libraries and experimental datasets.

items.title: LastWords: Boring Problems Revisited
items.abstract: In 2022, the second author published a Last Words piece in Computational Linguistics in which he pointed out that, despite the advances in AI up to that point, there were still some problems in natural language processing that on the one hand seemed trivial and perhaps boring, but on the other were hard to solve using purely neural methods. One such problem discussed in that context was text normalization, and a particular subproblem of that, namely number name reading. The piece came out just a few months before the first release of ChatGPT, and needless to say, a lot has happened since then. Indeed, as we document here, the problem (of number name reading) has practically been solved, at least by one of the latest frontier models. However, we believe that there are still open issues for such limited domain, constrained and limited resource problems, and that in some future machine learning approach, the massive resources of the latest frontier models would not be needed to solve them.

items.title: Leveraging extended reality and artificial intelligence for public speaking training in higher education: evaluating the impact of XR MALL on ESL/EFL students
items.abstract: This study examines the potential of XR MALL, an innovative application integrating Extended Reality (XR), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and mobile technologies to enhance public speaking skills among ESL/EFL students in higher education. Grounded in the Constructivist Approach and the Public Speaking Competence Model, a quasi-experimental design was employed with undergraduate students enrolled in an English presentation course at a Hong Kong university. Participants were assigned to experimental and control groups, with the experimental group using XR MALL over a ten-week intervention. Pre- and post-intervention data assessed presentation skills, language proficiency, public speaking anxiety (PSA), and cognitive and affective outcomes. Results indicated that students using XR MALL demonstrated significant improvements in self-perceived English proficiency, presentation skills, vocabulary, listening ability, and reductions in PSA compared to the control group. The experimental group also showed enhanced critical thinking, independent learning, confidence, and motivation. Students reported high satisfaction with the VR practice simulations and AI-powered speech feedback. The findings highlight the pedagogical value of integrating VR-based simulation, AI-driven feedback, and AR-supported vocabulary learning within a mobile-assisted framework. This study contributes to XR research by presenting a theory-driven, purpose-built mobile application that combines immersive practice and personalized feedback for public speaking training in ESL/EFL higher education contexts.

items.title: Leveraging Mental Models for Human-Centered Explanations: A Systematic Design Approach Illustrated by Explainable Fake Review Identification
items.abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) often prioritizes model fidelity over user intelligibility, yielding explanations that satisfy technical transparency yet fail to support human sense-making. We propose a human-centered approach, MIND-X (Mental-model INtegrated Design for eXplainability), which aligns explanations with users' mental models, commonsense concepts, and judgment heuristics. Using fake review detection as a case study, we contribute: (1) a qualitative study (n=10) that elicits how people assess review credibility and produces an actionable, design-guiding taxonomy of perceptual cues; (2) a set of design principles that link those cues to explanation strategies and prompt LLMs to generate adaptive, language-based explanations; and (3) a quantitative evaluation (n=166) showing that these explanations offer distinct advantages over token-level transparency methods widely used in explainable text classification in terms of understandability, satisfaction, perceived trust, persuasiveness, and decision-making support. Rather than claiming general superiority, our evaluation illustrates how grounding explanations in users' everyday reasoning practices can produce more intelligible and context-sensitive accounts. Our findings advance human-centered explanation design beyond a mere "gloss of transparency," demonstrating that a mental-model-aligned design process can improve intelligibility and support accountability across user-centered explanation tasks.

items.title: Lexical semantic development of high-frequency polysemous words in L2 writing: An LLM-assisted sense-level analysis
items.abstract: A key dimension of L2 writing development is learners’ ability to use words across a wider and more differentiated range of senses, yet this development remains difficult to capture at scale. This study proposes a scalable corpus-based approach to analyzing lexical semantic development at the sense level, using large language models for sense annotation and validating their performance against dictionary examples and human-annotated learner sentences. Focusing on 136 selected high-frequency polysemous lemmas, we compare sense distributions across 16 proficiency levels in EFCAMDAT with those in the written component of the BNC. Two main developmental patterns emerged. First, Jensen–Shannon distance between learner and native reference sense distributions decreased overall with proficiency, indicating increasing alignment with native reference usage. Second, entropy increased with proficiency, suggesting greater diversification of sense use. Exploratory item-level analysis showed that individual lemmas followed heterogeneous and sometimes non-linear trajectories, partly associated with differences in writing topic and genre. These findings suggest that L2 lexical development in writing involves not only changes in the frequency of word use but also the gradual expansion and differentiation of sense repertoires. The study also offers pedagogical implications for vocabulary instruction, writing development, and sense-aware assessment in second language education.

items.title: LIBERO-Pro2.0: A Benchmark for Evaluating the Robustness of Embodied Foundation Models
items.abstract: LIBERO has emerged as a widely adopted benchmark for evaluating robotic manipulation policies. However, strong performance on LIBERO does not necessarily indicate robust embodied capabilities, as models may exploit benchmark-specific regularities rather than generalize to diverse operating conditions. In this work, we introduce LIBERO-Pro2.0, a comprehensive benchmark for systematically evaluating the robustness of embodied foundation models under distribution shifts. LIBERO-Pro2.0 encompasses 22 static perturbations and 20 runtime interventions across six dimensions: Condition, Environment, Observation, Execution, Robot State Configuration, and Language, yielding 1,648 validated shifted task instances. To support robustness-oriented learning, we further collect 39,390 training trajectories through model-generated and human demonstrations. All shifted task instances undergo six rounds of iterative human review and correction to ensure physical plausibility and task validity. We evaluate 17 representative robot policies spanning vision-language-action models, world-action models, and robustness-oriented policies. Our results reveal substantial robustness gaps across all evaluated paradigms: under runtime distribution shifts, the evaluated models exhibit an average performance drop of 26.5 percentage points, with individual drops reaching 32.5 points. These findings highlight the gap between nominal benchmark performance and robustness under distribution shifts, underscoring the need for systematic robustness evaluation of embodied foundation models.

items.title: Limitations of Conventional Thyroid Collars and Emerging Design Solutions: A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Background: The thyroid gland is highly radiosensitive and is at considerable risk of occupational exposure in radiological and interventional procedures.Conventional thyroid collars are widely used due to their ability to attenuate scattered radiation; however, their design limitations may compromise both protective efficacy and user compliance in clinical settings.Objective: This narrative review aims to critically evaluate the limitations of conventional thyroid collars and synthesize emerging design solutions to improve radiation protection and ergonomic performance.Methods: A comprehensive narrative review was conducted using literature retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar.Studies published between 2000 and 2026 were included, focusing on shielding design, material properties, ergonomic factors, and radiation attenuation.Articles were selected based on predefined criteria, and findings were synthesized using a qualitative thematic approach and a total of 60 studies were included.Results: Evidence indicates that conventional thyroid collars, despite adequate attenuation, are limited by poor anatomical fit, leading to gaps and potential radiation leakage.Ergonomic challenges, including excessive weight, uneven load distribution, and thermal discomfort, contribute to reduced compliance and increased risk of musculoskeletal disorders.Additionally, collar design may interfere with imaging, particularly during thoracic CT examinations.Emerging solutions-such as anatomically contoured designs, lightweight lead-free materials, improved fastening mechanisms, and weight redistribution systemsdemonstrate enhanced fit, comfort, and usability.Conclusion: While conventional collars provide essential baseline protection, design-focused innovations are necessary to improve both safety and user compliance.Further standardization and clinical validation are required for broader implementation.

items.title: LLM Trojans that Increase Response Lengths and Cost
items.abstract: Management of the token-based costs of using LLMs has emerged as a significant problem. Some frontier-model providers charge five times per response token than per prompt token, while others offer prefilling discounts for prompt tokens. In this paper, we devise a defense against a new data-poisoning attack that plants a Trojan which increases the length of the response (and hence the cost to the user) when its trigger is present in the prompt. In particular, we demonstrate how a subtle Trojan may trigger on semantically similar instructions of an instruction fine-tuned LLM.

items.title: LLM-Based Evaluation Planning for Heterogeneous Optimization
items.abstract: Heterogeneous optimization problems require an optimizer to decide not only which candidate solutions to evaluate, but also which objectives and constraints should be evaluated under different costs and fidelities. Existing SOTA methods such as MFE-NSGA-III address this setting with manually designed selection metrics, but their behavior is largely determined by predefined heuristic rules and hyperparameters. In this work, we propose REP-HO, a reasoning-based evaluation planner that replaces the rule-based mixed-fidelity selection step with a large language model (LLM) planner. The LLM receives the same primitive optimization-state information as the heuristic planner, such as surrogate predictions, uncertainties, evaluation costs, and budget status. We first show that REP-HO achieves competitive performance compared to the human-designed metric-based method (MFE-NSGA-III). We then further enhance each decision with an adaptive nearest-neighbor summary, leading to better and more stable results. We evaluate REP-HO across five heterogeneous regimes covering cost imbalance, constraint difficulty, surrogate fidelity, budget level, and objective conflict. Across these regimes, one of the two variants obtains the best mean ranking score in every regime, REP-HO(Deepseek) is first or second throughout, and the planner shows adaptive allocation behavior, such as prioritizing constraint evaluations under tighter budgets and reallocating constraint evaluation budget when surrogate reliability changes. These results suggest that LLMs can serve as flexible evaluation planners for heterogeneous optimization, offering a general alternative to fixed hand-designed metrics.

items.title: Localizing AI in Rural India: The Role of Talent Management in Reconfiguring Agricultural Knowledge Systems
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into agriculture-focused development agendas, its use in rural field settings challenges current thinking about fit, equity, and sustainability. This paper examines the overlooked dimensions of how talent management processes impact the sociotechnical localization of AI in rural agricultural ecosystems in India. Based on multi-sited qualitative case studies in Karnataka, Bihar, and Maharashtra, we explore how talent pipelines, including agri-digital intermediaries, AI translators, and local facilitators, mediate the adoption, translation, and incorporation of AI tools by small institutional and professional farmers. The findings suggest that human infrastructure is not merely supportive but constitutive of the successful integration of AI, especially in settings characterized by educational asymmetries, caste hierarchies, and gendered exclusions. Informed by sociotechnical systems theory and the concepts of knowledge coproduction and epistemic justice, this research contends that talent management must be reimagined as a fundamental infrastructural and ethical spine for digital innovation. The analysis conceptualizes AI localization as a negotiated alignment between algorithmic systems and agrarian lifeworlds made possible by contextually embedded, culturally literate, and institutionally embedded human agents. This helps push the boundaries of what it means for AI to be technically feasible, socially situated, and democratically transformed in the Global South.

items.title: Managing the "Gig & Platform" Workforce: Psychological Contracts and Organizational Commitment Among Non-Traditional Workers in the Saurashtra Region of Gujarat State
items.abstract: With a focus on major urban-industrial centers—Rajkot, Jamnagar, Bhavnagar, and Junagadh—this study investigates the structural and psychological dynamics of platform labor in the Saurashtra region of Western Gujarat, India. Drawing on Psychological Contract Theory (Rousseau, 1989), we assess how worker perceptions of organizational obligations, transactional contracts, normative commitment, and turnover intentions are impacted by the transition from community-based informal employment to algorithmic management. Utilizing a convergent parallel mixed-methods design (N = 400 quantitative surveys; N = 28 qualitative interviews), the study evaluates digital platform governance (e.g., Zomato, Swiggy, Porter, Rapido, Urban Company) within localized socio-cultural matrices (siddhapana, local trade networks, informal credit dependency). Structural equation modeling demonstrates that algorithmic opacity and incentive volatility significantly induce Psychological Contract Breach (PCB). In turn, PCB severely reduces affective and normative commitment while increasing defensive continuance commitment and turnover intentions. Qualitative themes highlight collective counter-strategies, including coordinated app logouts and informal mutual-aid networks (bhaibandhi). Finally, policy and managerial interventions are outlined to foster sustainable platform governance in secondary urban hubs.

items.title: Mapping Generative AI, Consumer Behavior, and Digital Trust in Global Marketing
items.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is changing the way consumers search for information, evaluate alternatives, and make decisions in global markets. However, the literature remains fragmented between disciplines, application areas, and geographic contexts, limiting a coherent understanding of consumer responses to GenAI. This study reviews 49 peer-reviewed articles indexed in Scopus and published between 2020 and 2026. Following the PRISMA guidelines, the articles were selected through a systematic selection process and examined using descriptive analysis and thematic synthesis. Five main areas emerge: human–AI interaction and interface design, AI-driven marketing and personalization, consumer psychology and decision-making, predictive analytics infrastructures, and ethics, governance, and responsible AI. Across these areas, trust and perceived control consistently shape consumer responses to GenAI. They can evolve through interaction and influence whether personalization is perceived as useful and engaging or as intrusive and difficult to control. The findings also suggest that TAM and UTAUT provide only a partial explanation of consumer responses to generative AI, given the conversational, adaptive, and increasingly agentic nature of large language models. Based on these findings, the study develops a framework connecting technological, psychological, marketing, and governance factors, with implications for both research and responsible AI deployment across diverse global contexts.

items.title: Mapping the Intellectual Capital Research Landscape: A Bibliometric Analysis of Trends, Contributions, and Future Research Directions
items.abstract: Intellectual capital has become an important source of value creation and competitive advantage in knowledge-intensive economies, where organizational performance increasingly depends on the effective use of knowledge-based and other intangible resources. This study maps the development and structure of intellectual capital research through a bibliometric analysis of publications indexed in the Scopus database. The search strategy used combinations of keywords relating to intellectual capital, human capital, structural capital, intangible assets, and value added. After the application of publication-type, subject-area, and language filters, the final dataset comprised 787 English-language journal articles. Publication trends, journal distribution, institutional and country contributions, influential documents, co-citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence, and international collaboration were examined using Excel, VOSviewer, R, and Biblioshiny. The findings show a marked expansion of intellectual capital scholarship, particularly from 2015 onward, with annual scientific production reaching 84 articles in 2024. The 787 articles were distributed across 306 journals, while the Journal of Intellectual Capital was the leading publication outlet in the dataset. India recorded the highest number of publications among the countries listed, whereas Taiwan had the highest total citations in the country-level citation comparison. Highly cited foundational studies and co-citation patterns point to the continuing influence of work on intellectual capital measurement, including the Value Added Intellectual Coefficient (VAIC) approach. Keyword co- occurrence revealed interconnected themes concerning intellectual capital and firm performance, human and structural capital, relational capital, knowledge management, innovation, intangible assets, disclosure, and value creation. The collaboration map also indicates cross-country research links, although the distribution of contributions varies across institutions and regions. Overall, the study provides a structured overview of the intellectual capital research landscape and identifies opportunities to extend the field through stronger cross-country collaboration, broader measurement approaches, and greater attention to contemporary issues such as artificial intelligence, digital transformation, financial distress, and the strategic management of intangible resources. These directions may help researchers develop a more integrated understanding of how intellectual capital is measured, deployed, and associated with organizational outcomes.

items.abstract: Internal degradation due to moisture and thermomechanical stress in zinc oxide (ZnO) surge arresters increases leakage current, leading to failures in distribution systems. Although contemporary monitoring relies on harmonic analysis or thermal imaging, there is an absence of artificial intelligence models powered by geometric properties of the voltage-current (V-I) curve, such as the hysteresis loop area. Consequently, this scoping review maps literature techniques to attest to this gap and support the application of physics-based variables in the fault diagnosis of these devices.

items.title: Marketing to Machines: Strategic Frameworks for Engagement with Autonomous Agentic AI
items.abstract: The evolution of Generative AI from passive recommendation engines into autonomous Agentic AI is fundamentally redefining the landscape of consumer decision-making and value creation. As consumers increasingly delegate choice evaluation, dynamic negotiation, and purchasing execution to software agents, traditional marketing paradigms centered on human psychological persuasion are losing their strategic effectiveness. This chapter critically examines the emerging dynamics of "Marketing to Machines" (M2M), proposing a comprehensive conceptual model, the Algorithm-to-Algorithm (A2A) Engagement Framework, to illustrate how modern enterprises can strategically align their market offerings with autonomous machine buyers. To build this framework, we conduct an integrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature published between 2015 and 2026 across marketing strategy, information systems, computer science, and behavioral economics, selected through systematic topic-based sampling. The synthesis reaches key theoretical and practical conclusions across four structural dimensions: the transition from emotional branding to structured data and metadata optimization (Generative Engine Optimization), the mechanics of real-time machine-to-machine value negotiation, the restructuring of traditional brand equity into algorithmic trust, and the ethical alignment of enterprise offerings with automated choice architectures through transparent governance and data integrity. The chapter embeds an explicit ethical framework to evaluate algorithmic neutrality, fairness, and consumer regulatory compliance. To demonstrate real-world applicability, the conceptual model is grounded in an analytical examination of established commercial autonomous agent environments and digital governance protocols. Ultimately, the conclusions of this chapter indicate that long-term competitive advantage in an agent-dominated market relies heavily on data machine-readability, operational transparency, API-driven fulfillment, and ethical algorithmic reputation management, providing actionable guidance for re-engineering Go-To-Market strategies when the primary buyer is an autonomous algorithm.

items.title: Medical Fine-Tuning Reshapes, Not Reduces, Patient-Facing AI Risk: A Rubric-Based, LLM-Judge Evaluation Framework
items.abstract: Patient-facing medical question answering with large language models (LLMs) is moving from research demonstrations to production deployments, yet evaluation remains anchored on factual correctness. Factuality is necessary but not sufficient: a response can be factually grounded and still issue a directive that, if acted on, would harm the patient. We introduce a risk-sensitive evaluation framework that scores responses by the presence and severity of six categories of risk-bearing language (treatment directives, contraindications, dosage expressions, urgency-triage cues, high-alert medication mentions, and overconfident assertions), anchored on published clinical harm taxonomies. Severity is classified by a three-judge LLM ensemble. We apply this framework to six 7-9B instruction-tuned models, three general (Mistral-7B, Phi-3.5-mini, Llama-3.1-8B) and three medically adapted (BioMistral-7B, OpenBioLLM-Llama3-8B, Med42-Llama3-8B), on 200 real patient questions from the K-QA benchmark. Two findings emerge. First, ensemble risk-bearing language is statistically independent of factual hallucination rate (pooled Spearman $ρ= -0.065$, $n = 300$, 95% CI $[-0.18, +0.05]$; distance correlation $= 0.10$, independence test $p = 0.24$). Second, medical fine-tuning does not reduce aggregate risk but reshapes it: continued-pretraining adaptations (BioMistral, OpenBioLLM) consistently suppress high-alert medication mentions while amplifying overconfident assertions, whereas clinical instruction-tuning (Med42) suppresses dosing only, without amplifying overconfidence. Per-category Krippendorff $α$ is fair to good for the four linguistically anchored categories (0.53-0.71) and low for the two clinical-judgment-dependent categories (0.19, 0.31), indicating where automatic safety evaluation is and is not yet reliable. We release the rubric, judge prompts, and evaluation code.

items.title: Medical visual analytics as an integrated interaction system for primary care patient data exploration
items.abstract: Primary care physicians must build an overview of complex patient histories within short consultations. Clinical information is often distributed across systems, visits, and temporal events, while the physician still has to maintain situation awareness, patient communication, and clinical accountability. Medical Visual Analytics systems seek to reduce search effort, while their acceptance depends on more than the available visual modules. The interface has to fit clinical tasks, human perception, user preferences, and the workflow of the practice. This work presents a Medical Visual Analytics concept and prototype architecture for primary care. Building on HCI, visual perception, and visual analytics task abstraction, the publication structures the system around clinical tasks, interaction behavior, workflow context, patient data, and visual representation. The implemented prototype connects patient configuration, a clinical data model, service-based data access, an interactive dashboard, anatomical body-based views, and optional MediChat assistance into one physician-centered system. The focus is not autonomous diagnosis, but a source-verifiable environment that helps physicians find, relate, inspect, and correct patient information. The contribution is an HCI-oriented system design that treats interaction, visual prioritization, and source access as design mechanisms intended to support acceptance and clinical usability. Content, layout, visual variables, and interface orchestration are discussed as adaptation targets that respond to user role, task abstraction, interaction behavior, patient-data characteristics, and consultation phase. Building on prior conference work on visual decision support for primary care, this journal extension reframes the system as a user-centered Medical Visual Analytics environment and discusses how such adaptation is intended to reduce search time, support perception, and preserve physician control in everyday outpatient work.

items.title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
items.abstract: The adoption of Large Language Models for radiology report structuring has been largely dominated by either proprietary cloud-based models or large open models requiring high-end GPUs for deployment, which is a critical bottleneck for clinical adoption in radiology workflows that demand data privacy and offline operation. To address this, we present MedPAO-Assist, an edge-deployable agentic framework that generates structured radiology reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands, requiring only $\approx3.3$ GB peak RAM and achieving an average end-to-end latency of $\approx31$ seconds on a standard laptop CPU through an asynchronous, multi-threaded execution pipeline. The system currently supports four major imaging modalities -- Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI. To our knowledge, it is among the earliest agentic systems to run its entire pipeline with a Small Language Model (SLM) in the 0.6B-parameter range. This multi-agent architecture, built around an Extract-Ground-Generate paradigm, performs concept extraction, SNOMED-CT grounding, and structured report generation, followed by a speech-driven human-in-the-loop correction phase, together forming a fully "no-touch" reporting workflow that requires no keyboard input, external API calls, or internet connectivity. We evaluate each pipeline stage individually -- concept extraction, ontology grounding, and concept categorization and report hardware profiling results demonstrating the system's feasibility for real-time, CPU-only clinical deployment.

items.title: MELD: Recursive Self-Improvement via Hierarchical Coordination for Multi-Agent Scientific Discovery
items.abstract: Multi-agent scientific discovery with large language models raises a coupled learning problem: research assignments determine both which experiments are pursued and the experiences from which agents adapt. We introduce MELD, a unified hierarchical test-time training framework that jointly adapts a team-level Coordinator policy and agent-level individual Scientist policies within a single discovery process. The Coordinator generates a joint portfolio of search branches and research directives over a shared derivation tree, while Scientists develop hypotheses and execution plans implemented by a shared frozen Executor. Both levels receive alternating GRPO-style parameter updates under a shared smooth best-of-budget objective, allowing team organization and individual research behavior to co-evolve in a recursive self-improvement loop. Our analysis establishes objective alignment for the hierarchy, characterizes conditions for coordination gains over independent parallel discovery and the first-order benefit of private adaptation, and derives a finite-budget regret bound for adapted models. On 22 MLGym and MLE-bench tasks, MELD is best on 20 of them and achieves the highest aggregate normalized scores on MLGym, using a 4B backbone for coordination and research. Most baselines use proprietary Scientists, and all systems share one frozen Executor.

items.title: Metaphysical Nūr And Generation Alpha: Technology, Ontology, and the Crisis of Orientation
items.abstract: Purpose - This study examines the Islamic metaphysical concept of Nūr (light) as an ontological and epistemic framework for understanding the technological condition of Generation Alpha. The purpose is to clarify the distinction between technological illumination—characterized by visibility, access, and informational abundance—and orienting illumination, understood as intelligibility, guidance, and meaning. By doing so, the paper seeks to address the growing crisis of orientation affecting younger generations in digitally saturated environments. Methods - The research adopts a qualitative, theoretical, and interdisciplinary methodology. It combines hermeneutic analysis of Qurʾānic texts and classical Islamic philosophy with conceptual analysis drawn from contemporary philosophy of technology, media theory, pedagogy, and AI ethics. Institutional statistical data from international organizations are used descriptively to contextualize the analysis, without serving as primary empirical evidence. Results - The study demonstrates that contemporary digital technologies generate unprecedented levels of illumination in the form of constant visibility and exposure yet lack intrinsic orientational capacity. This form of technological illumination differs structurally from Nūr, which functions as a principle uniting manifestation, intelligibility, and guidance. As a result, digital environments tend to amplify information while weakening meaning, discernment, and interior integration, particularly in the formative experiences of Generation Alpha. Conclusions - The paper concludes that Nūr, employed as a non-confessional metaphysical heuristic, provides a robust ontological criterion for distinguishing between exposure and guidance, correctness and wisdom. This framework offers significant pedagogical and ethical implications for education, writing, and the use of artificial intelligence, emphasizing the need to reorient technological practices toward discernment, interiority, and meaningful human understanding.

items.title: Methodology for the application of generative artificial intelligence tools in higher design education
items.abstract: The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) technologies across both theoretical and practical domains is fundamentally transforming the epistemological and pedagogical foundations of higher design education. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of the methodological integration of generative AI tools, including ChatGPT, Claude, Midjourney, and DALL·E, in fostering creative thinking, critical analysis, and practical skills among design students in higher education institutions. The research examines the transition of studio pedagogy from traditional forms toward hybrid and dialogical models, the reinterpretation of Donald Schön’s concept of reflection-in-action within algorithmic environments, and the evolving role of the educator in AI-assisted learning processes. Methodologically, the study is grounded in a modified Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework and a four-component Information and Communication Competence (ICC) model. The findings indicate that the systematic and purposeful implementation of GAI tools can increase students’ visual design production and productivity by approximately 14%; however, it may also lead to reduced diversity of ideas and an overreliance on algorithms for cognitive functions. To mitigate these risks, the study proposes the concepts of epistemic vigilance and process-oriented hybrid assessment mechanisms as essential components of contemporary design education.

items.title: Miasma: an open-source, lightweight countermeasure against unauthorized AI web scraping
items.abstract: The widespread adoption of large language models has greatly increased demand for publicly accessible web data, resulting in increased web scraping across the internet. The resulting bandwidth and compute costs fall on site operators rather than on the parties collecting the data, with scientific databases and journals among those reporting service disruption [1]. Existing mitigations such as rate limiting, CAPTCHAs, and robots.txt rules can discourage well-behaved crawlers, but impose no cost on scrapers that choose to ignore them. Deception-based alternatives have shown promise, though prominent examples such as Cloudflare’s AI Labyrinth remain tied to enterprise platforms [2]. Separately, recent work suggests that small quantities of poisoned content can compromise a model [3], and that continual training on low-quality content measurably degrades model performance [4]. Miasma is an open-source tarpit that brings a deception-based defense within reach of small operators. Implemented in Rust, it runs as a standalone service or as an embeddable library, trapping unwanted crawlers in a recursively generated network of links whose pages carry deliberately poisoned content. Miasma does not perform bot detection itself. Rather, it is paired with an upstream mechanism such as hidden links or an existing detection tool, and its poisoned content is drawn from a configurable external source. Instead of blocking requests outright, Miasma reduces the value of what is collected while keeping its own operational footprint small. To that end, Miasma uses asynchronous request handling on the tokio runtime, a bounded in-flight request cap that places a hard limit on memory consumption, and a custom HTML templating system that streams page chunks without allocating intermediate strings. Miasma is able to serve 100 sustained in-flight requests while using roughly 50 MB of memory. Across six months of deployment on a small portfolio site, Miasma served 210 million requests and 1.29 TB of poisoned content. As of October 2026, the project has reached 1,200+ stars and 6 contributors on GitHub, with 6,500+ Docker pulls, and is distributed under GPL-3.0 via Cargo, Docker, and community-maintained packages.

items.title: MisleadQA: Diagnosing LLM Failures under Misleading Context
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used to answer questions from retrieved or user-provided context. However, provided context can be factually true yet out-of-scope, describing a different entity, time, or location from the one the question targets, and still lead models to a wrong answer. Prior work has mainly studied factually false or irrelevant context. It remains unclear whether such out-of-scope context misleads models as much as false context, and whether adding gold context prevents models from being misled by either. We introduce **MisleadQA**, a diagnostic dataset of multiple-choice questions with an abstention option. Each question pairs gold context (G) with true but out-of-scope context (S) and false but in-scope context (F) supporting the same wrong answer. We evaluate six open-weight LLMs. On questions they answer correctly without context, providing S alone leads them to switch to this wrong answer in 29.3% of cases, and providing F alone does so in 75.4%. Adding G nearly removes the effect of S, but F still misleads models in 21.0% of cases, especially when F comes first. A context-faithful instruction reduces these errors mainly through abstention and lowers accuracy even with G. These findings suggest that evaluations should check whether context applies to the question, not only whether it is true, and should report correct, misled, and abstention rates together. Data and code are available at [https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MisleadQA](https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MisleadQA).

items.title: ML-Based Intrusion Detection System with Intrusion Prevention System
items.abstract: This paper presented a hybrid rule-based and machine-learning system that intercepts navigation at the browser and blocks phishing, malware, ransomware, and DGA-style malicious destinations in real time, without requiring network-level packet capture. A Random Forest classifier trained on eight lexical and structural URL features reached 95.83% accuracy and a 95.52% F1-score on a held-out test set, at an inference cost of under 6 ms per request, well within the latency budget of a normal page navigation. More importantly, a real false-positive failure was found, measured, and fixed: restricting an entropy rule from the full URL to the hostname alone, combined with removing a spurious pattern from the training corpus, reduced false blocks on ordinary websites from 7 of 10 to 1 of 12 with no loss of true detections. A live per-attack-type accuracy view complements the usual offline benchmark by scoring every trained algorithm against real traffic as it happens, and a per-class confusion matrix shows the two remaining error types clearly enough to prioritize future work: at the current dataset scale, missed detections (2 of 34) matter more than false alarms (1 of 38), which argues for growing the malicious-class training data before anything else. Taken together, these results suggest that a browser-level hybrid detector is a practical, lightweight complement to network-level intrusion detection for the individual users and small deployments that flow-based systems do not reach.

items.title: Modeling the Coevolution of Human Skills and AI Adoption
items.abstract: The value of relying on generative AI depends on two quantities that evolve with its use: users' unaided skill, which may decline without practice, and the originality of AI-assisted work, which may decline as more people rely on similar tools. We model this process as a coevolutionary game in which individuals choose between autonomous and AI-assisted work, with autonomous practice strengthening their skills while reliance on AI gradually erodes them. When the reinforcing effect of skill erosion outweighs the crowding cost of lost originality, the population exhibits two alternative stable states: low AI adoption with high average skill, and high AI adoption with low average skill. Because skill is individual, autonomous workers remain more skilled than AI users, making autonomous work less vulnerable to population-wide skill decline. The strength of this effect is governed by a timescale ratio: the rate at which skills adapt relative to the rate at which individuals change strategy. The same ratio determines the full distribution of skills, which we derive analytically. Populations with identical AI adoption and average skill can differ sharply: when strategies change frequently, skills remain homogeneous and collective lock-in to high AI adoption is stronger; when strategies persist, lock-in weakens but the population can polarize into highly skilled autonomous workers and AI-dependent individuals. Modeling output overlap further shows that more diverse AI outputs can make widespread adoption harder to reverse. Together, these results expose tradeoffs between the benefits of widespread AI adoption and its long-run risks, making collective lock-in and skill polarization distinct intervention targets.

items.title: MODERN MEDICAL EDUCATION: PEDAGOGICAL TRENDS AND HEALTH OF PARTICIPANTS OF THE EDUCATIONAL PROCESS
items.abstract: Introduction. The modern system of medical education is undergoing active transformation under the influence of globalization, rapid development of medical technologies, and the digitalization of the educational process. The implementation of innovative approaches, including simulation-based learning, artificial intelligence technologies, as well as virtual and augmented reality, contributes to improving the effectiveness of training medical professionals. At the same time, the intensification of the educational process and the digitalization of the learning environment may affect the psycho-emotional state and health of participants in the educational process, which determines the need to analyze current pedagogical trends in medical education. Aim. To analyze modern pedagogical trends in medical education and determine their impact on learning effectiveness and the health of participants in the educational process. Materials and methods. An analytical review of scientific publications by domestic and foreign authors devoted to the development of medical education, the implementation of digital technologies in the educational process, and studies examining the influence of the educational environment on the psycho-emotional state of students and teachers was conducted. Methods of system analysis, generalization, and comparison of the results of contemporary scientific research were used. Results. It was established that the integration of innovative educational technologies contributes to improving the quality of training of medical professionals, the development of clinical thinking, and the formation of practical skills. At the same time, the increasing academic workload, the digital intensity of the educational process, and the need for continuous professional development may lead to higher levels of stress, emotional exhaustion, and professional burnout among participants in the educational process. Conclusions. Modern medical education requires a balanced combination of innovative pedagogical technologies and approaches aimed at preserving the mental and physical health of participants in the educational process. A promising direction is the development of health-preserving educational strategies, optimization of academic workload, and the implementation of trauma-informed approaches in the system of medical education.

items.title: Multi-agent collaborative semantic recognition and real-time event generation for power grid alarm monitoring
items.abstract: Massive alarm data from grid monitoring systems is essential for secure power dispatch operation. Aggregating discrete alarm signals into structured events is vital to enhance grid monitoring intelligence. Nevertheless, existing event rule bases adopt domain-customized complex grammar with diverse symbolic expressions, making traditional string matching methods unable to achieve accurate semantic parsing. This paper proposes a multi-agent collaboration-based method for semantic recognition and real-time generation of power grid monitoring alarm events. The method integrates large language models (LLMs), knowledge graph (KG) representation learning, and multi-agent coordination to realize high-precision semantic understanding and real-time intelligent generation of alarm events. Specifically, three original contributions are made: (1) a three-layer standardized preprocessing pipeline combined with instruction tuning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that bridges the semantic gap between domain-specific rule grammar and LLMs; (2) a dual-drive fusion recognition model integrating GraphSAGE-based knowledge graph embedding and BiLSTM temporal encoding with an attention fusion mechanism; and (3) a hierarchical multi-agent collaborative architecture with explicit communication protocols, conflict resolution strategies, and a SEEN (Semantic Event Exception Notifier) algorithm for unknown event detection. Experimental results on 356,950 real alarm samples from a regional power grid demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an F1-score of 96.9% and a false alarm rate of 4.2%, outperforming conventional rule matching methods by 25.3% points under signal-loss scenarios. Ablation studies confirm that each module contributes independently and significantly to the overall performance.

items.title: Multi-Agentic AI for Intent-Driven and Conflict-Aware rApp Policy Orchestration in Open RAN
items.abstract: Open radio access network (O-RAN) enables a multi-vendor ecosystem that accelerates xApp development for near-real-time (RT) network management. However, this openness shifts a combinatorial coordination burden to the Non-RT layer, where rApp policies compose xApps from a growing catalog to realize operator intents. Coexisting intents further compound this challenge, as conflicts may arise among xApp actions, rApp policies, and their cross-layer interactions. To maximize intent admission while maintaining key performance indicator (KPI) compliance across incoming and incumbent intents, we propose a large language model-based Multi-Agentic AI framework. A Reasoning Agent screens candidate xApps against KPI contracts and produces a joint intent admission and xApp assignment decision. On post-deployment KPI violations, a Diagnosis Agent identifies the root causes of failure, labels the conflict mechanism, and guides the Reasoning Agent in subsequent attempts. Experimental results show that the framework based on GPT-OSS 120B achieves 28.6% more KPI-compliant cases and admits over 15* as many incoming intents as state-of-the-art baselines. Under the Qwen 72B variant, Diagnosis increases compliant cases by 50.0%, quadruples admitted intents, and reduces deployment attempts by 32.6%. A live deployment conforming to O-RAN specifications further validates the feasibility of the proposed solution for conflict-aware rApp policy orchestration in real networks.

items.title: Multi-horizon vessel trajectory prediction with a physically constrained TCN–KAN framework
items.abstract: Accurate vessel trajectory prediction is essential for maritime situational awareness, traffic management, and autonomous navigation. However, existing data-driven methods often struggle to simultaneously represent temporal dependencies at different scales, nonlinear maneuver-induced deviations, and kinematic consistency, particularly as the forecasting horizon increases. This study proposes TCN–KAN–PINN, a unified framework combining a multi-scale causal Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), a parallel Linear-KAN predictor, and physics-informed training. The TCN encoder uses hierarchical dilated residual blocks and sample-specific scale fusion to extract complementary temporal features from historical AIS observations. The Linear Base Pathway models the dominant motion trend, whereas the KAN Residual Pathway learns nonlinear corrections associated with vessel maneuvers. A time-discretized kinematic residual further penalizes discrepancies between predicted coordinate increments and expected displacements derived from vessel motion states, while Relative Loss Balancing with Random Lookback (ReLoBRaLo) adaptively balances the data and physics objectives. The model directly generates a complete 30-step future trajectory, with the 5 min, 15 min, and 30 min results evaluated as prefixes of the same output. Experiments on a real-world AIS dataset show that the proposed framework achieves the best overall trajectory accuracy among representative kinematic and deep learning baselines while maintaining favorable speed and course consistency and practical inference efficiency. Results reported as mean ± standard deviation over five independent runs indicate stable predictive performance. Ablation studies further show that kinematic supervision benefits prediction from the early forecasting steps, whereas the contribution of the KAN pathway becomes more pronounced at medium and long horizons.

items.title: Multiclass Software Defect Prediction Using an Optimized LLM CodeSentinel-BERT Based Framework
items.abstract: The prediction of software defects is important to detect defects in source codes prior to their deployment but traditional techniques use selected features and limited binary classification. This research work proposes DefectGuard, a transformer-based multiclass software defect prediction system for C/C++ source code that utilizes CodeBERT fine-tuning. This custom dataset consists of 2,000 samples of manually collected and labeled C/C++ source codes and includes nine classes of defects, namely syntax, semantic, logic, linker, and runtime-related defects. The proposed pipeline includes preprocessing, stratified splitting, sub-word tokenization, CodeBERT representation learning, and multiclass classification. The experimental results show the accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score of 98.8%, 96.4%, 95.8%, and 96.1%, respectively, on the test set. Additionally, ROC-AUC and confusion-matrix metrics are used to evaluate the class-level discrimination. Moreover, the proposed model is implemented in a real-time Flask-based web application, which can classify the source code into defect labels with confidence scores and language detection to provide the interpretation feedback.
